The issue was that when a route function's return annotation was `type(None)` (the class `NoneType`), `get_typed_annotation` in `fastapi/dependencies/utils.py` returned `type(None)` instead of `None`. In `fastapi/routing.py`, this value was treated as truthy, leading to the creation of a `response_field` and a subsequent `AssertionError` when the status code was `204 No Content`, as response bodies are not allowed for that status code.

I modified `get_typed_annotation` to explicitly return `None` if the annotation is either `None` or `type(None)`. This ensures that the `response_model` is correctly set to `None`, preventing the generation of an unnecessary response body in the OpenAPI schema and avoiding the `AssertionError` for `204 No Content` responses.

The fix was verified using a reproduction script that confirmed `route.response_model` is `None` when the return annotation is `type(None)`.
